idiom_name: object declaration (lazily initialised, exactly one instance)
implementation_notes: Kotlin has the pattern in the language: an object declaration creates the class and its single instance in one step, initialises it lazily on first access, and the specification describes it as introducing a type with a single global value. Members are reached through the object's name, so no private constructor and no getInstance() are involved; data object (1.9+) adds equals/toString for the stateless singleton. Use by lazy for a lazily created top-level or companion property when the instance needs constructor arguments, and use a companion object for factory-style members rather than as a singleton holder.
pitfalls: Initialisation runs under the class-initialisation lock: heavy or blocking work in the object's initialiser stalls every thread that touches Config afterwards.
Objects are per class loader: Android class loaders, OSGi bundles, hot reload or duplicate library copies each hold their own instance.
A global var in an object is not synchronised on Kotlin/JVM; keep the singleton immutable or guard mutations explicitly.
by lazy defaults to LazyThreadSafetyMode.SYNCHRONIZED - PUBLICATION may run the initialiser several times and NONE provides no guarantee, so the mode is part of the contract.
